title: ZA-2026-1432-CUB-1A
text:
ZA-2026-1432-CUB-1A  Council District: 11 – Park
  CEQA: ENV-2026-1433-CE  Last Day to Act: 12-28-26
  Plan Area: Palms – Mar Vista – Del Rey

  PUBLIC HEARING REQUIRED

  PROJECT SITE:  12904 – 12910 West Palms Boulevard

  PROPOSED PROJECT:
  A Conditional Use to permit the sale and dispensing of a full line of alcoholic beverages for on-site
  consumption in conjunction with an existing 3,194 square foot restaurant which includes an existing 998
  square-foot outdoor patio and 750 square-foot sidewalk dining area.

  APPEAL:
  An appeal of the September 29, 2026, Zoning Administrator’s Determination which:
  1. Determined, based on the whole of the administrative record, that the Project is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines, Section 15301, Class 1
  (Existing Facilities), and there is no substantial evidence demonstrating that any exceptions contained
  in Section 15300.2 of the State CEQA Guidelines regarding location, cumulative impacts, significant
  effects or unusual circumstances, scenic highways, or hazardous waste sites, or historical resources
  applies;
  2. Approved, pursuant to Section 12.24 W.1 of the Los Angeles Municipal Code, a Conditional Use to
  permit the sale and dispensing of a full line of alcoholic beverages for on-site consumption in conjunction
  with an existing restaurant in the [Q]C1-1 Zone; and
  3. Adopted the Conditions of Approval and Findings.

  Applicant:  Jeremy Adler, 3rd Place, LLC, Beethoven Market
  Representative: Laurette Healey, City Land Use Inc.

  Appellants:  1. Azadeh Hawkins

  2. Barrett Hawkins

  3. Boris Feldman

  Staff:  Esther Ahn, City Planner
  esther.ahn@lacity.org
  (213) 978-1486

  Christina Toy Lee, Associate Zoning Administrator
summary: The West Los Angeles Area Planning Commission will hear appeals of a Zoning Administrator approval that lets a restaurant at 12904–12910 West Palms Boulevard in Palms serve a full line of alcohol for on-site drinking. The appellants challenge that approval and the environmental exemption that went with it.
